key_insight: Federated learning can potentially predict breast cancer tumour progression using multimodal patient data while keeping data stored locally across institutions.
clinical_relevance: This approach may enable privacy-preserving, personalised treatment planning and support future decision tools such as digital twins in breast cancer care.
method: Trained a federated learning model on multimodal inputs including clinical, biomarker, demographic, and MRI data.
Compared federated performance against a centralised model built from aggregated data.
Examined deployment pillars such as transparency, scalability, security, and fairness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a direct comparison between federated and centralised learning to assess whether privacy-preserving training can achieve comparable predictive performance.
watch_item: Real-world use still depends on secure model updates, consistent performance across patient subgroups, and smooth deployment across multiple institutions.
paper_title: Trustworthy Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Federated Learning for Personalised Breast Cancer Prediction
